Write Arrow C streams into tables

Source: R/arrow.R
zugodb_arrow.Rd

DBI::dbWriteTableArrow() creates a table from an Arrow C stream, or replaces one (overwrite = TRUE) or adds to one (append = TRUE); DBI::dbAppendTableArrow() adds a stream's rows to a table that exists; DBI::dbCreateTableArrow() creates an empty table from an Arrow schema. Any producer of the Arrow C stream interface works: a stream handle of class nanoarrow_array_stream, as zuarrow, nanoarrow, arrow and 'ADBC' drivers make, or a data frame, which zuarrow::arrow_stream() converts (zuarrow is then needed). The stream is read once, one batch at a time, and released: it cannot be read again.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'zugodb_connection'
dbWriteTableArrow(
  conn,
  name,
  value,
  ...,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  append = FALSE,
  temporary = FALSE
)

# S4 method for class 'zugodb_connection'
dbAppendTableArrow(conn, name, value, ...)

# S4 method for class 'zugodb_connection'
dbCreateTableArrow(conn, name, value, ..., temporary = FALSE)

Arguments

conn

A zugodb_connection.

name

The table's name, as for DBI::dbWriteTable().

value

For dbWriteTableArrow() and dbAppendTableArrow(), an Arrow C stream handle (class nanoarrow_array_stream) or a data frame. For dbCreateTableArrow(), a schema handle (class nanoarrow_schema), or a stream handle, data frame or format string, which zuarrow::arrow_schema() reads a schema from.

...

Not used.

overwrite, append

TRUE to replace or to add to a table that exists; at most one of them.

temporary

Not supported: the engine has no temporary tables.

Value

dbWriteTableArrow(), dbCreateTableArrow(): TRUE, invisibly. dbAppendTableArrow(): the number of rows written.

Details

A new table's columns take these engine types:

ArrowEngine
booleanBOOLEAN
int8TINYINT
int16, uint8SMALLINT
int32, uint16INTEGER
int64, uint32, uint64BIGINT
float, doubleFLOAT, DOUBLE
string, large string, string viewVARCHAR
binary, large binary, binary view, fixed-size binaryBLOB
date32, date64DATE
timestamp, any unit and time zoneTIMESTAMP, the instant in UTC

Another Arrow type (a decimal, a time of day, a duration, an interval, a list, a struct, a map, a union, a dictionary, an extension type, the null type, a half float) is a zug_type_error naming the column, raised from the stream's schema before any row is read. So is a value its column cannot hold: a uint64 past 2^63 - 1, a timestamp with a fraction of a microsecond, a string that is not valid UTF-8 or holds a NUL. An append matches columns by name, as DBI::dbAppendTable() does, and converts as it does (a whole double into an INTEGER, say).

A load that fails part-way, by such a value, by the producer's own error (a zug_stream_error carrying its message) or by an interrupt, leaves nothing: a new table is removed, and an append or an overwrite reads the stream into a staging table first, so that the table it writes is only changed once the whole stream has been read. The engine has no transactions, so this costs a copy of the rows.

Examples

con <- DBI::dbConnect(zugodb())
stream <- zuarrow::arrow_stream(head(mtcars))
DBI::dbWriteTableArrow(con, "cars", stream)
DBI::dbAppendTableArrow(con, "cars", tail(mtcars))
#> [1] 6
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT count(*) AS n FROM cars")
#>    n
#> 1 12
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
